title: VR Live Events
desc: Plan and run a live virtual-reality or virtual event: platforms, access, moderation, safety and measures of success.
outcomes: Prepare tech checks and run sheets.
task: Plan and run a 30-minute virtual event for 10 to 20 people, with rehearsal, moderation, accessibility, feedback and report.
condition: Computers or VR headsets as available, a free event platform, two peers and a mentor.
standard: Rehearsal passes; moderation rules enforced; accessibility options present; feedback from 80% of attendees; report with data; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Event planners, teachers, community groups, trainers.
evidence: plan, run sheet, tech checklist, feedback report
modules: Formats, platforms and fit
Understand
A virtual event can run on a flat screen, a headset or both. The best format is the one your audience can use.
Desktop 3D spaces and video rooms are easiest to join.
Headsets give presence but need equipment, space and comfort checks.
Hybrid events stream a live room to virtual guests.
Check bandwidth, device ownership and time zones.
A training session uses a desktop 3D room so that every learner can join from a laptop. A product launch offers a headset option to early adopters after a survey shows 5 per cent own headsets.
Compare three formats for one event goal.
Table includes device needs, access and cost.
Goals, audience and plan
Create
Define success before choosing tools.
Write one goal with a number, such as 60 attendees with 70 per cent staying to the end.
Write a one-page event plan: audience, format, date, agenda, roles and budget.
Plan how guests join: link, app or invitation.
Prepare an event page with what to expect.
A community group aims for 60 attendees and a 4 out of 5 satisfaction score. It sends one link 24 hours before and a reminder one hour before.
Write goals and a one-page plan.
Goals are measurable and the plan covers roles and timing.
Technical checks and fall-backs
Apply
Test everything on real devices before the event.
Accounts, links, audio, avatars and screen sharing.
Test on each device type and connection speed.
Prepare a backup video link and a helper desk.
Record known issues and fixes.
A fallback video link saves a session when the 3D room fails to load for ten attendees.
Make a ten-item checklist and test it on three devices.
Checklist is tested and issues are logged.
Moderation and safety
Evaluate
Virtual spaces need clear rules and active moderators.
Code of conduct; tools to mute, block and report.
Age rules, parental consent for minors and no sharing of personal data.
Trained moderators with a script: warn, mute, remove, report.
Keep an incident log.
A disruptive participant is muted, removed and reported according to the code. The log records time, action and follow-up.
Write rules, a moderator script and an escalation plan.
Rules are clear and tested in a mock session.
Accessibility and comfort
Evaluate
Everyone should be able to take part.
Captions, transcripts and keyboard options.
Motion-sickness settings: teleport movement, short sessions and breaks.
Time zones, language and sign-up form questions about needs.
Alternatives for those without headsets.
Teleport movement and 10-minute breaks reduce discomfort for headset users. A form asks about captions and break needs.
Write an access plan.
Measures cover vision, hearing, motion and device access.
Run sheet and rehearsal
Apply
Smooth delivery needs a minute-by-minute plan.
Roles: host, tech, moderator, content lead.
Rehearse twice with real devices and record it.
Plan transitions and time for questions.
Keep a printed copy of the run sheet.
A rehearsal reveals audio echo; the host uses headphones for the live run. A 30-second silence at the start is cut.
Run a rehearsal and log fixes.
Fixes are logged and the second rehearsal is clean.
Live run
Create
Deliver your pilot event calmly.
Welcome, rules, content, Q and A, close.
Handle problems calmly and use the helper desk.
Collect feedback and record attendance.
Keep a live issue log with times.
The pilot finishes on time with 14 attendees and three technical issues, all solved within 5 minutes.
Run the pilot event.
Mentor observes and signs the run.
Measure, report and improve
Analyse
Learn from the data.
Attendance, time in event and feedback scores.
Fix the top issues and plan the next event.
Send a thank-you and a survey within 24 hours.
Share a one-page report.
Average rating 4.3 out of 5 and 80 per cent stayed to the end. The report lists three fixes.
Write the report.
Report has numbers, feedback and three dated improvements.
quiz: Name a format.
Desktop 3D, headset VR or hybrid. (Covered in module 1: Formats, platforms and fit. To pass that module: Table includes device needs, access and cost.)
Why a fallback?
Protect the session. (Covered in module 3: Technical checks and fall-backs. To pass that module: Checklist is tested and issues are logged.)
Code of conduct use?
Set behaviour rules. (Covered in module 4: Moderation and safety. To pass that module: Rules are clear and tested in a mock session.)
Motion sickness fix?
Teleport movement or breaks. (Covered in module 5: Accessibility and comfort. To pass that module: Measures cover vision, hearing, motion and device access.)
Time zone issue?
Choose fair times. (Covered in module 5: Accessibility and comfort. To pass that module: Measures cover vision, hearing, motion and device access.)
Metric?
Attendance or rating. (Covered in module 8: Measure, report and improve. To pass that module: Report has numbers, feedback and three dated improvements.)
Roles?
Host, tech, moderator. (Covered in module 6: Run sheet and rehearsal. To pass that module: Fixes are logged and the second rehearsal is clean.)
Rehearsals?
At least two. (Covered in module 6: Run sheet and rehearsal. To pass that module: Fixes are logged and the second rehearsal is clean.)
Privacy?
No personal data sharing. (Covered in module 4: Moderation and safety. To pass that module: Rules are clear and tested in a mock session.)
Access feature?
Captions. (Covered in module 5: Accessibility and comfort. To pass that module: Measures cover vision, hearing, motion and device access.)
